RE:
Docket No. 25-45-GE - The Narragansett Electric Company d/b/a Rhode Island Energy
Application for Approval of a Change in Electric and Gas Base Distribution Rates
Pursuant to R.I. Gen. Laws §§39-3-10 and 39-3-11
Dear Ms. De La Rosa:
Enclosed for filing with the Public Utilities Commission ("PUC") is an original and ten copies
of the Company's1Application for a Change in Electric and Gas Base Distribution Rates Pursuant to
R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 39-3-10 and 39-3-11.
The Company is proposing a two-year rate plan. For the first year of the proposed rate plan,
the Company is requesting an increase in electric and gas base distribution rates to recover the costs
incurred to operate the electric and gas distribution systems on a safe and reliable basis for customers.
The Company is requesting a base distribution rate increase of approximately $65.9 million for the
electric system and approximately $114.7 million for the gas system. For the second year of the
proposed rate plan, the Company is requesting an increase of approximately $17.6 million for the
electric distribution system and approximately $3 l .8 million for the gas distribution system.2
Recovery of the costs to operate the systems is necessary for the Company to maintain and repair
distribution infrastructure, maintain a qualified and dedicated workforce, and deliver the quality
service that customers expect. The Company is committed to its role as the elect and natural gas
service provider in Rhode Island arid takes seriously its obligations to provide energy infrastructure
essential for Rhode Island's economy to grow and for customers to obtain safe, reliable, and
affordable utility service.
The Company's filing encompasses elements that are critical to maintaining the Company's
ability to provide its customers with the high level of service that they expect. If approved by the
PUC as fled, the proposed rate increases would result in an increase of 4.8 percent on the total
monthly bill for the typical Narragansett Electric residential customer consuming 500 kwh monthly
1 The Narragansett Electric Company d/bt"a Rhode Island Energy ("Rhode Island Energy" or the "Company").
2 The Company also is providing data regarding revenue requirements for a third year as required by the approved
Amended Settlement Agreement from the Company's last base distribution rate case in Docket No. 4770. The Company
is not, however, seeking approval of a rate change to go into effect for that third year.

for the first year of the proposed rate plan and 0.9 percent for the second year of the proposed rate
plan. For Narragansett Gas, the increase on the total annual bill for the typical residential heating
customer consuming 845 therms annually would be 20.6 percent for the first year of the rate plan and
4.4 percent for the second year of the proposed rate plan.
This Application also contains specific proposals that relate to the Company's recovery of
costs, including for example:
Information Technology ("IT") Investments: The Company, in collaboration with PPL
Corporation and its other affiliates, has planned several IT investments that will:
(i) provide greater customer service support and improve the overall customer experience,
(ii) streamline and simplify security, including cybersecurity, (iii) increase efficiency of
the Company's day-to-day operations, (iv) streamline and improve the back-office
operations that provide support to the Company, and (v) address on-premises servers,
storage, network devices, communications equipment, mobile workforce, and office
devices that must be replaced because they are out of date.
Electric Low-Income Discount Rate: The Company is proposing a redesign of its low-
income discount rate for electric customers to provide greater relief to the customers who
need it most, while preserving the best practices associated with current implementation of
this rate. As part of that effort, the Company has developed a customer outreach plan to
engage with customers and increase awareness of the low-income discount rate.
Effective Date of New Rates
Consistent with the provisions ofR.I. Gen. Laws § 39-3-11 and 810-RICR-00-00-1 .10(C) of
the PUC's Rules of Practice and Procedure, the enclosed proposed tariffs have an effective date of
January 1, 2026. The Company prepared its case with the expectation that the PUC would suspend
the effective date of the proposed rate changes for a period of up to eight months and has designed the
new rates for the first year of the proposed rate plan to recover the proposed cost of service over the
twelve-month rate-year period beginning August l, 2026 .

APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL OF A 
 
 
 
DOCKET NO. 25-45-GE 
CHANGE IN ELECTRIC AND GAS 
BASE DISTRIBUTION RATES 
 
NOTICE TO CUSTOMERS OF FILING AND CHANGE IN RATE SCHEDULES 
 
On November 26, 2025, pursuant to Rhode Island General Laws Sections 39-3-10 and 39-3-11 
and the Rhode Island Public Utilities Commission’s (the “Commission”) Additional 
Requirements for Filings of General Rate Schedule Changes, 810-RICR-00-00-5, The 
Narragansett Electric Company d/b/a Rhode Island Energy (“Rhode Island Energy” or the 
“Company”), a subsidiary of PPL Corporation, filed with the Commission a comprehensive 
filing to change its base distribution rates for its electric distribution (“Narragansett Electric”) 
and gas distribution (“Narragansett Gas”) operations in Rhode Island proposed to take effect on 
January 1, 2026.  
 
As part of its request for a change in base distribution rates, the Company is requesting approval 
of certain ratemaking proposals designed to recover the costs of serving customers, including 
those relating to: necessary staffing for all aspects of its operations for providing service to 
customers; investments in improved information technology; facilities investments; cost 
recovery procedures for major storm events; an improved low-income discount for income-
eligible customers; and planned development of future time-varying rate designs for electric 
distribution rates.  The Company currently is operating under the terms of the Amended 
Settlement Agreement approved by the Commission in RIPUC Docket No. 4770 (2017) for 
Narragansett Electric and Narragansett Gas.   
In its filing, Rhode Island Energy seeks to implement a two-year rate plan.  In the first year of the 
rate plan, the Company’s preliminary proposed base distribution rates are designed to collect 
additional operating revenue in the amount of $180,667,638 to support total revenue 
requirements of $428,749,820 for electric and $430,309,514 for gas.  In the second year of the 
rate plan, the Company’s preliminary proposed base distribution rates are designed to collect 
additional operating revenue in the amount of $49,373,017 to support total revenue requirements 
of $446,363,395 for electric and $463,143,492 for gas. 
 
For Narragansett Electric, in the first year of the proposed rate plan, the proposed rates would 
increase annual operating revenue by approximately $65.9 million, or 18.2 percent, with varying 
impacts on individual customer bills.  Generally, the total monthly bill impact for a typical 
residential electric customer using 500 kilowatt-hours per month would be an increase of 4.8 
percent, or $7.78 per month.  Electric commercial and industrial customers would experience 
total monthly bill impacts ranging from a decrease of approximately 1.0 percent to an increase of

approximately 5.0 percent. In the second year of the proposed rate plan, the proposed rates would 
increase annual operating revenue by an additional approximately $17.6 million, or 3.6 percent, 
with varying impacts on individual customer bills.  Generally, the total monthly bill impact for a 
typical residential electric customer using 500 kilowatt-hours per month would be an additional 
increase of 0.9 percent, or $1.56 per month.  Electric commercial and industrial customers would 
experience total monthly bill impacts ranging from an additional decrease of approximately 0.2 
percent to an additional increase of approximately 2.0 percent. 
 
For Narragansett Gas, in the first year of the proposed rate plan, the proposed rates would 
increase annual operating revenue by approximately $114.7 million, or 36.4 percent, with 
varying impacts on individual customer bills.  Generally, the total annual bill impact for a typical 
residential gas heating customer consuming 845 therms annually would be an increase of 20.6 
percent, or $343.53 per year.  Gas commercial and industrial customers would experience total 
annual bill impacts that will range from an increase of approximately 7.2 percent to 
approximately 30.2 percent.  In the second year of the proposed rate plan, the proposed rates 
would increase annual operating revenue by an additional approximately $31.8 million, or 7.4 
percent, with varying impacts on individual customer bills.  Generally, the total annual bill 
impact for a typical residential gas heating customer consuming 845 therms annually would be 
an additional increase of 4.4 percent, or $89.43 per year.  Gas commercial and industrial 
customers would experience total annual bill impacts that will range from an additional increase 
of approximately 1.9 percent to approximately 6.3 percent. 
 
The Commission can suspend the rates for up to eight months from the proposed effective date. 
No rate change will take effect until the Commission has conducted a full investigation and 
hearing on the proposal.  The Commission will publish a notice of the hearing dates when they 
are scheduled.  Customers may comment on the proposed rate increases at that time.
